chapter: Lester Young and the early Basie years
title: Prez not a good businessman; Flip Phillips's lighters
summary: Tate tells Prez he is a legend who does not take care of business; he repays favors.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: You know, "Let's review the books." (Laughter.) So he says, "I haven't done so well, you know." I says, "What do you mean?" He says, "I never really made it on my own ." I said, "What do you mean, you haven't made it?" I says, "Man, you're a legend." I says, "You and Hawk." He says, "Yeah, but all the other ladies that they say play like me make all the money." So I says, "Well, I don't think you're a good businessman, I'll tell you that now." I says, "But you could have made it. I can even book you. All the world knows you and nobody have trouble --" I says, "But maybe you just don't take care of business," because he'd mess up at Small's , he had fallen off the stage, which wasn't like Prez. He'd gotten high and then fallen off the stage and they fired him and things like that.

So he found out that Norman GranZ was like giving him 500 and some of the others was getting 14 and Bean and them was getting 14. You see, to tell you about Prez, if you once do him a favor, he never stop paying you back. Everytime he'd think of something -- Flip told me he got nine cigarette lighters that Prez had given him, all cigarette --
Because he'd fix his horn, he fix his horn for him all the time. He'd come to Flip and say, "Lady

My baby ain't acting right." They'd be on a jazz -- said, "You better do something for her." And Flip said he was standing over him watching him / "Look now, Prez, if I'm going to fix it, take your ass on in the other room somewhere." He says, "I know what the fuck I'm / Leave me alone."
